title: Human reproduction and gametogenesis; Chromosomes, karyotypes and genome organisation
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: CD05b#t3 term and clue written for the game; CD05b#t2 term and clue written for the game; RP01a#t1 term and clue written for the game; CD05b#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: CD05b#N.3, RP01a#N.7, RP01a#N.10, RP01a#N.13.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Alleles
items.clue: Different versions of the same gene

items.label: Loci
items.clue: The positions of genes on a chromosome

items.label: Acrosome
items.clue: Sac of digestive enzymes in the head of a sperm.

items.label: Homologous pair
items.clue: Two matching chromosomes, one from each parent, of the same size

questions.stem: A person has two different alleles of the ABO blood group gene, which has its locus on chromosome 9. Where are these two alleles in one of the person's body cells?

options.text: One on each chromosome 9 of the homologous pair, at the same locus on each.
Both on the same chromosome 9, side by side at two neighbouring loci.
On chromosome 9, at a locus that varies from one person to another.
Only one allele is in a body cell; the other allele is found only in gametes.

questions.explanation: Homologues carry the same genes at the same loci. One allele came from each parent, on that parent's chromosome 9.

questions.stem: Which pairing correctly matches an adaptation of a human gamete to its function?

options.text: Egg cytoplasm with nutrient stores: supplies the embryo's first divisions.
Sperm acrosome: stores the fuel that the mitochondria respire while the sperm swims.
Egg zona pellucida: a cell wall that gives the egg mechanical protection from damage.
Egg and sperm of matching size: each gamete carries half of the chromosomes needed.

questions.explanation: The egg is large because its cytoplasm contains stored nutrients (yolk droplets) that supply the embryo during its first divisions, before it can obtain nutrients from the mother.

questions.stem: In an experiment, eggs treated so that they could not carry out the cortical reaction were each entered by several sperm. Which explanation is correct?

options.text: Without the cortical reaction the zona pellucida is not hardened, so further sperm can still digest through it and fuse.
The cortical reaction is what lets the first sperm in, so blocking it should have stopped fertilisation altogether.
Sperm bore through the egg membrane with their enzymes, so hardening the zona could not have stopped them.
Only one sperm normally reaches the egg, so the treatment must somehow have attracted extra sperm to it.

questions.stem: In a fish species the female lays a few hundred large eggs in a nest and the male releases many millions of tiny sperm over them. Which statement explains the difference in size and number?

options.text: Eggs are larger because each one carries far more of the genetic material than a sperm does.
The numbers should be equal since one sperm fertilises one egg; the surplus sperm are defective ones.
Sperm are small because so many are made that only a little cytoplasm is available for each one.
Sperm must travel to the eggs, so they are small with few food reserves and can be produced cheaply in vast numbers.
